svg.title: The nudges multiply
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing a curve with a red secant line through two points a distance h apart converging to a green tangent as h shrinks; a contour map with a red arrow pointing straight uphill perpendicular to the contour and a green arrow pointing the opposite way; a chain of three function boxes f, g and h with blue forward arrows carrying values left to right and red backward arrows carrying local derivatives right to left, with the product dL/dx equals dL/db times db/da times da/dx written beneath; a comparison of forward mode needing n separate passes against reverse mode needing one backward sweep; and a U-shaped plot of finite-difference error against step size with the optimum marked at h equals one times ten to the minus four.
svg.text: a derivative is the slope of a nudge
and it is always perpendicular to the contour you are standing on
THE CHAIN RULE: forward values, backward gradients, same graph
backward: dL/dx = dL/db x db/da x da/dx
the nudges MULTIPLY along the chain. That is all backpropagation is.
and if you check it numerically
gradcheck at 1e-7. Measured worst relative error 1.8e-10
(MSE) to 2.9e-9 (5-deep tanh chain). If it fails your
gradient is wrong - not your learning rate.
